feature: Where a frame of the hour-long timeline's zoom goes, measured whole
summary: Nothing on screen changed in this pass. The speed walk now says how busy the main thread is on each frame of a timeline zoom or scroll, and can profile every pass of those frames. That showed even a frame that paints nothing near the whole-hour view keeps the main thread busy for about 8 ms of its 8.3, so the next step is structural, not another trim.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The button on step 1 opens your own copy of the 60 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev; File > Open reaches it too (Cmd-Shift-G, ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev). Measured with a timeline-only speed walk on the probe; the lanes-taking-turns trial was A/B on one build by a throwaway switch, two runs each way.

try.do: Open the 60 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below.
Pinch the timeline in and out quickly near the whole-hour view, then stop.
Scroll the timeline end to end with two fingers.

evaluate: Does a pinch near the whole-hour view feel the same as yesterday's build (it should: nothing the app does changed)?
Is moving the track lanes onto layers of their own, slid and stretched outside the view updates, the right next step for this task?
rough: Numbers on the final build, 60 minute edit: near Fit 11.18 ms a frame (held 9.25, painted afresh 13.87), zoom in 10.55, zoom out 9.72, scroll 8.86 (p95 12.9, worst 23). New: main thread busy a frame near Fit 8.98 ms, zoom in 8.20, zoom out 7.08, scroll 7.07. Baseline at the start of the pass on the same code: near Fit 11.39, zoom in 11.08, zoom out 9.69, scroll 9.48.

Where a near-Fit frame goes (every pass profiled): an update pass of 5.4 ms on a frame that holds every painting (lane bodies 1.3 ms spread thin, SwiftUI graph upkeep 1.6), a layout and drawing pass of 1.9 ms, and a trail of small passes. A frame that lays its pictures adds about 2.7 ms. Written into docs/design/video.md.

Tried and backed out: lanes taking turns to let go of a held painting, three groups each on a step of its own. Pictures laid near Fit fell from 2.4 a frame to 1.8, but the loop stayed at 11.0 to 11.6 ms against 10.9 to 11.3, every frame near 11 ms instead of one in three near 15.
Pass 17's next step, laying pictures off the main thread, would save about 1.1 ms a frame near Fit at most and leave a held frame's 8 ms, so it was not built.
Bars of the task not reached: 95 per cent of zoom and scroll frames under 8.3 ms and none over 16, and edits within 16 ms. The task stays open.
No mock covers the timeline's speed; nothing about the timeline's look changed.
